newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report - Australia carries India, not Egypt.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report - Australia carries India, not Egypt.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said it had not sold wheat to Egypt in its 500,000 tonne tender but confirmed it had sold to India.

AWB said in its weekly grain market report the big news of the past week was the sale of 500,000 tonnes of French wheat by the European Union for February/March shipment at US$142.00-$144.00 a tonne fob
The trade had speculated about AWB sales of 400,000 tonnes in addition to the EU sale, AWB said.
The AWB denied this, saying that instead it had sold about 125,000 tonnes of wheat to India.
This followed comments by an AWB official on Friday that sourcing in Egypt's latest purchase of 110,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian wheat for June delivery had not yet been confirmed.
The AWB also said in its weekly report that Argentina's statement that about 7.5 million tonnes of its record wheat crop of 16.0 million tonne crop had been sold for export came as a surprise.
"The market maintains that this estimate is overestimated by at least a million tonnes," AWB said.

Early, last week Jordan bought 100,000 tonnes of Argentina wheat on a C&F basis at the equivalent of about A$145.50 fob, while India also purchased 100,000 tonnes for February shipment at about A$172.00 a tonne, it said.
Prospects for Australia's sorghum crop improved with good rains over the growing region.

Part of the AWB's A$4.00 a tonne pool price increase last week was because of the softening Australian dollar but a continuing good rate of sales was holding pool returns and allowing the AWB to capture any upside in the market, it said.
The AWB had shipped about 5.5 million tonnes of an anticipated 18.0 million tonnes of exports for 1996 season wheat, with 10.0 million tonnes priced, it said.

It confirmed statements by AWB chairman Trevor Flugge at last week's Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics conference that the first estimate of pool returns for the coming season for Australian Standard White was A$170.00-A$180.00 a tonne, or A$10.00-A$22.00 a tonne below the current estimated equity for 1996/97 pools.
Domestic feed grain prices continued to climb over the past week with stocks on farm limiting available supplies, it said.
Feed barley prices last week rose by up to A$12.00 a tonne in Victoria, with triticale jumping by A$6.00 and feed oats rising A$9.00 a tonne, all reflecting the demand/supply balance.
The AWB estimate of the national wheat crop remains at 23 million tonnes.
